<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<span class="ltx_author_before"> and </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Wenwu Zhu
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id19" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_institution">Tsinghua University</span>, <span id="id20" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_city">Beijing</span>, <span id="id21" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_country">China</span>
</span></span></span></span></div>
<div class="ltx_dates">© none</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract.</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Long video understanding (LVU) is challenging due to rich and complicated multimodal clues in long temporal range. Current methods adopt reasoning to improve the model’s ability to analyze complex video clues in long videos via text-form reasoning. However, the existing literature suffers from the fact that the text-only reasoning under fixed video context may exacerbate hallucinations since detailed crucial clues are often ignored under limited video context length due to the temporal redundancy of long videos.
To address this gap, we propose <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Video-TwG</span>, a curriculum reinforced framework that employs a novel <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">T<span id="abstract1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">hink-</span>w<span id="abstract1.1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">ith-</span>G<span id="abstract1.1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">rounding</span></span> paradigm, enabling video LLMs to actively decide when to perform on-demand grounding during interleaved text–video reasoning, selectively zooming into question-relevant clips only when necessary. Video-TwG can be trained end-to-end in a straightforward manner, without relying on complex auxiliary modules or heavily annotated reasoning traces.
In detail, we design a Two-stage Reinforced Curriculum Strategy, where the model first learns <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> behavior on a small short-video GQA dataset with grounding labels, and then scales to diverse general QA data with videos of diverse domains to encourage generalization. Further, to handle complex <span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> reasoning for various kinds of data, we propose TwG-GRPO algorithm which features the fine-grained grounding reward, self-confirmed pseudo reward and accuracy-gated mechanism.
Finally, we propose to construct a new TwG-51K dataset that facilitates training.
Experiments on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU show that Video-TwG consistently outperforms strong LVU baselines. Further ablation validates the necessity of our Two-stage Reinforced Curriculum Strategy and shows our TwG-GRPO better leverages diverse unlabeled data to improve grounding quality and reduce redundant groundings without sacrificing QA performance.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Video Reasoning, Video Grounding, Reinforcement Learning
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1. </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Long video understanding (LVU) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu and Krahenbuhl, 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib64" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> has become a cornerstone for real-world multimodal information access. Users increasingly pose natural-language questions about movies, vlogs, news, and instructional videos, expecting accurate answers grounded in long-form video content. Recent benchmarks further push LVU toward realistic, hour-scale videos and compositional reasoning, exposing substantial gaps in current video large language models (LLMs) with respect to long-horizon perception and reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Many works address LVU from multiple perspective and achieve good performance, such as long context modeling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024e</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ren et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, memory-centric designs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Santos et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Diko et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, token compression <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meng et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tao et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, adaptive sampling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, video agent pipelines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025e</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ren et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e.t.c</span>.
Since long videos contain rich and complicated multimodal clues in long temporal range, recent video reasoning LLMs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> benefit from test-time-scaling via conducting text-form reasoning to better analyze the complex video clues, which contributes to LVU significantly. However, they conduct text-only reasoning under fixed video context, suffering from hallucinations since the important detailed information might be ignored under limited video context length due to the temporal redundancy of long videos, where only a few sparsely distributed moments are relevant for answering a given question, and thus, achieve sub-optimal results.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To address this problem, we propose <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Video-TwG</span>, a curriculum reinforced framework where we employ a novel <span id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">T<span id="S1.p3.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">hink-</span>w<span id="S1.p3.1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">ith-</span>G<span id="S1.p3.1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">rounding</span></span> paradigm, which equips video LLMs with explicit on-demand video grounding behavior during reasoning, without relying on complex auxiliary modules or costly supervised fine-tuning reasoning traces. As shown in Fig. <a href="#acmlabel1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, instead of passively reasoning from a fixed, statically sampled video context, our method follows the insight of Retrieval-Augmented-Generation (RAG) and iteratively decides what evidence it needs next and issues grounding actions to zoom into query-relevant video clips with fine-grained representation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18702v1/concept-level-v2.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/177;" width="476" height="177" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>. </span><span id="S1.F1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Conceptual level comparison between our Video-TwG and existing video reasoning models. The frame with <span id="S1.F1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">blue</span> triangle means the important detail for this question. Existing reasoning models reach the wrong answer via reasoning on missed video context, while we address it via leveraging grounding during reasoning to dynamically perceive important clues.</span><span id="acmlabel1" class="ltx_acm_description ltx_centering ltx_nodisplay"></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In details, our Video-TwG mainly contains the following parts. To reduce the training difficulty, we propose a Two-stage Reinforced Curriculum Strategy. In the first stage, the model learns <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> paradigm on easier, short-video GQA data. In the second stage, the training scales to general QA data on videos of various domains and duration, where grounding labels are largely unavailable. In this stage, the model is encouraged to generalize its <span id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> ability to richer scenarios. Furthermore, to handle the complicated reasoning trajectories for various kinds of data, we propose the TwG-GRPO algorithm, where we assign the fine-grained grounding reward for GQA data, and specifically design the self-confirmed pseudo reward for large amounts of general QA data to encourage high-quality grounding actions, and we apply the accuracy-gated mechanism to avoid the optimization conflicts between accuracy and grounding targets.
To support our training, we propose to construct TwG-51K, a novel dataset which combines (a) a small subset of video GQA data with grounding annotations and (b) a large collection of unlabeled general video QA data for generalization purpose.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Empirically, without relying on heavily annotated reasoning traces for supervised fine-tuning, Video-TwG consistently outperforms strong baselines across three mainstream benchmarks after two-stage curriculum training: Video-MME <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, LongVideoBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and MLVU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Compared to Qwen2.5-VL-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, our model achieves improvements of 7.0, 5.3, and 7.1 under low-resolution inputs, and 2.5, 3.9, and 5.0 under high-resolution inputs on these benchmarks, respectively.
Ablation study validates the necessity of our Two-stage Reinforced Curriculum Strategy and shows that our TwG-GRPO effectively helps the model to learn <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> from various data, especially in unlabeled data. It’s noted with the self-confirmed pseudo reward, the model learns to conduct grounding actions more adaptively, improving the grounding quality and reducing grounding actions by 15.7% without sacrificing QA performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, our contributions are fourfold:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose Video-TwG, a curriculum reinforced framework that enables video LLMs to iteratively think with grounding for long video understanding, without heavy external modules or costly supervised reasoning traces.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce a Two-stage Reinforced Curriculum Strategy to reduce the training difficulty and TwG-GRPO, a novel algorithm which combines fine-grained grounding rewards, self-confirmed pseudo rewards, and an accuracy-gated mechanism to jointly improve answer correctness and grounding quality.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct a new dataset, TwG-51K, which can facilitate the training through providing both labeled and unlabeled data.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Extensive experiments on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU show consistent advantages over strong LVU baselines.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2. </span>Related Works</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1. </span>Long Video Understanding</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Long video understanding (LVU) is the fundamental cornerstone for real-life applications and is quite challenging for current video LLMs.
Recent LVU methods mainly fall into the following directions.
(i) Long-context modeling scales video LLMs to longer inputs via architectural/efficiency improvements <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024e</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ren et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> with hour-scale attempts.
(ii) Memory-centric designs maintain learnable or external memory to accumulate salient cues over time <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Santos et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Diko et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
(iii) Token compression reduces the cost of long sequences <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meng et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tao et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>.
(iv) Adaptive sampling selects informative frames/clips under budget <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and highlights "needle-in-a-haystack" temporal localization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Meanwhile, realistic benchmarks like MLVU expose persistent length-induced degradation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
(v) video agent systems decompose the long video question into several intermediate steps and design cascaded pipelines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025e</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ren et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>
Above all, the insight is to model long-range relations among multimodal cues and allocate computation to the most informative parts of long videos.
This motivates our Video-TwG framework that enables video LLMs to invoke on-demand grounding during reasoning: reasoning interprets complex cues, while grounding pinpoints the most relevant video clips.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2. </span>Video Reasoning</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent "test-time scaling" suggest that allocating more computation at inference can further unlock LLM capabilities. Among this, LLM reasoning (e.g., CoT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022</a>)</cite>/ToT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2023</a>)</cite>) has shown clear scaling benefits for solving complex problems, and recent work further demonstrates that post-training with reinforcement learning can substantially strengthen reasoning behaviors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Building on these advances, video reasoning emphasizes producing process-like intermediate traces, like stepwise rationales, to improve output quality and interpretability, rather than only emitting final answers, to better grasp multimodal cues and analyze their relations.
Current post-training reasoning methods, often RL-flavored, encourage models to produce more faithful, verifiable reasoning traces, especially for temporal understanding cases <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025d</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>.
Besides, new datasets/benchmarks provide reasoning-trace supervision for video understanding and analysis, showing that temporal localization and evidence alignment remain key bottlenecks for current video LLMs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nagrani et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pei et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
However, most works optimize text-form reasoning under fixed video context, which doesn’t work well in LVU due to its high temporal redundancy, whereas our Video-TwG triggers dynamic grounding actions during reasoning to retrieve and zoom into most relevant clips, letting the reasoning enhance perception.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3. </span>Video Grounding</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Video grounding localizes the start and end timestamps of a clip that semantically matches a natural-language query <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anne Hendricks et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lan et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib70" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024c</a>)</cite>.
With the rise of Video LLMs, grounding is increasingly used to test whether models can consistently point to temporal evidence rather than only generate plausible descriptions.
Recent works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zeng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pramanick et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jung et al., 2025</a>)</cite> advance Video-LLM grounding by improving temporal referencing and grounded training/evaluation, yielding better accuracy on standard benchmarks.
Different from the query-only setting, we treat video grounding as an RAG-style retrieval step conditioned on the Video-LLM’s accumulated video-text reasoning context.
At each step, the model first retrieves the most relevant clip given the video and prior reasoning, then re-loads the grounded clip with fine-grained representation into the context to support subsequent reasoning.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3. </span>Video-TwG Framework</h2>

<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18702v1/trajectory-v2.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/136;" width="476" height="136" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>. </span><span id="S3.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The trajectory of <span id="S3.F2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span>. Initially, the coarse-grained video and question are given and in each turn, the model gives a thinking process and an action based on the history interaction. If the action is grounding, the grounded video clip is zoomed in with a fine-grained representation and added to the context. If the action is answering, the reasoning process stops.</span><span id="acmlabel2" class="ltx_acm_description ltx_centering ltx_nodisplay"></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1. </span>Preliminary</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our framework formulates <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> to multi-turn dialog.
Given a question <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> and a video <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>, the video LLM <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> is required to give its answer <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{a}</annotation></semantics></math> in a reasoning chain consisting of grounding(<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>) and answering(<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>) actions along with thinking process(<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>) in a maximum of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> turns. The <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th turn is formulated to:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(1)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{k},g_{k})\ \text{or}\ (t_{k},{a})=\mathcal{M}(V,p,t_{1},g_{1},v_{1},p_{1},...,t_{k-1},g_{k-1},v_{k-1},p_{k-1})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>or</mtext><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t_{k},g_{k})\ \text{or}\ (t_{k},{a})=\mathcal{M}(V,p,t_{1},g_{1},v_{1},p_{1},...,t_{k-1},g_{k-1},v_{k-1},p_{k-1}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},...,p_{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},...,p_{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math> are prompts for initial and intermediate turns containing the question <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> and the task instruction. In each turn, video LLM <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> takes the interaction history as input and outputs the next thinking <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and action, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i. e.</span> grounding action <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> or answering action <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{a}</annotation></semantics></math>. The thinking <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, grounding action <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> and answering action <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{a}</annotation></semantics></math> are in the format of</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E2X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="S3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">After each turn with the grounding action, the grounded video clip <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is concatenated to the history.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2. </span>TwG-51K Dataset Construction</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To facilitate training, we construct the TwG-51K dataset, comprising 50,744 multiple-choice video QA samples in total. Among these, 8,195 samples have ground-truth question-relevant video grounding annotations, while 42,549 samples lack such annotations.
(i) For samples with video grounding annotations, we collect Grounded Question Answering (GQA) data from NExT-GQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and CG-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, where the video clip that contains important clues for the answer are annotated. NExT-GQA provides 10.5K explicit grounding annotations, and we filter out samples whose videos are shorter than 20 seconds and finally obtain 7,123 samples from NExT-GQA. CG-Bench features long videos between 10 and 80 minutes with video grounding annotations, which consists of 12,129 questions from 1,219 videos. We collect videos from CG-Bench-mini and filter out samples where the IoU between the ground-truth video grounding clip and the entire video is smaller than 0.01 to facilitate training, and finally obtain 1,072 samples.
(ii) To scale and diversify training data, we randomly sample a subset of LLaVA-Video-178K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2024b</a>)</cite>, a commonly used multi-domain general video instruction tuning dataset consisting of 1.3M questions from 178K videos, and finally obtain 42,549 multiple-choice training samples.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3. </span>Multi-Grained Video Representation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the initial video is to provide global clues while the dynamically grounded video is to provide detailed information, we adopt multi-grained video representation for different videos.
For the initial video input <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>, we represent it with <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\text{coarse}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext>coarse</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\text{coarse}}</annotation></semantics></math> frames and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{coarse}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>coarse</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{coarse}}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per frame in a coarse-grained way, while <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\mathrm{fine}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>fine</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\mathrm{fine}}</annotation></semantics></math> frames and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\mathrm{fine}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>fine</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\mathrm{fine}}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per frame in a fine-grained way for the dynamically grounded video segment <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> (generally, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\mathrm{coarse}}&gt;F_{\mathrm{fine}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>coarse</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>fine</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\mathrm{coarse}}&gt;F_{\mathrm{fine}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\mathrm{coarse}}&lt;f_{\mathrm{fine}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>coarse</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>fine</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\mathrm{coarse}}&lt;f_{\mathrm{fine}}</annotation></semantics></math>).
To better support videos with various durations and reduce the search scope, in the grounding action, the start and end frames are the frame indexes in the initial video representation, <span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i.e.</span> from 0 to <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\mathrm{coarse}}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>coarse</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\mathrm{coarse}}-1</annotation></semantics></math>. When cutting the corresponding video clip, they are converted into real seconds.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4. </span>Two-stage Reinforced Curriculum Strategy</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the base video LLM is not capable of benefiting from the <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> stably, to reduce the training difficulty, we design a two-stage curriculum. For the first stage, we train the model with short video GQA data with grounding labels, <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i.e.</span> NExT-GQA part in TwG-51K, serving as cold start, to activate the model to follow the <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> pattern and reach the answer via zooming in the correct video clip. Next, for the second stage, we train the model on the entire TwG-51K dataset, most of which lack grounding labels, to improve the model’s generalization via thinking with adaptive grounding.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We skip the SFT and adopt curriculum reinforced learning for both stages, since the model is observed to have the potential to think with grounding, which is demonstrated in subsequent experiments. Benefiting from our RL-only solution, our Video-TwG can be easily improved without heavy SFT annotation works in a lighter way.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5. </span>TwG-GRPO Algorithm</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.5. TwG-GRPO Algorithm ‣ 3. Video-TwG Framework ‣ Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, we propose a TwG-GRPO algorithm to support RL training in various data, which is based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, for the sake of memory-friendly nature. We adopt multi-turn optimization with trajectory-level reward for computation efficiency, where a trajectory <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> turns follows the format: [{user: <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>},{assistant: <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>,<math id="S3.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="0em">OPEN</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> },{user: <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>},…,{assistant: <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math> },{user: <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math> },{assistant: <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> , <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> }]. For each sample, we collect rollouts and Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 3.5. TwG-GRPO Algorithm ‣ 3. Video-TwG Framework ‣ Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows the rollout process in our multi-turn <span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> setting.
After rolling out, we follow the GRPO algorithm to calculate the trajectory advantages in the group:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(\{R_{j}\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(\{R_{j}\})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(\{R_{j}\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(\{R_{j}\})</annotation></semantics></math> is the mean and standard deviation of the rewards in each group. The policy video LLM model is optimized by:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\triangleq\frac{\mathcal{M}_{\theta}(\tau_{i}\mid q)}{\mathcal{M}_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\tau_{i}\mid q)},\qquad\bar{r}_{i}(\theta)\triangleq\operatorname{clip}\!\big(r_{i}(\theta),\,1-\epsilon,\,1+\epsilon\big)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>≜</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≜</mo><mpadded style="width:1.428em;" width="1.428em"><mi>clip</mi></mpadded><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>r</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\triangleq\frac{\mathcal{M}_{\theta}(\tau_{i}\mid q)}{\mathcal{M}_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\tau_{i}\mid q)},\qquad\bar{r}_{i}(\theta)\triangleq\operatorname{clip}\!\big(r_{i}(\theta),\,1-\epsilon,\,1+\epsilon\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E4Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mi>GRPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Besides, we deploy dynamic resampling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> technique when a group does not provide valid learning signals to improve training stability and accelerate convergence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Since vanilla accuracy and format rewards can not handle complex <span id="S3.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">think-with-grounding</span> reasoning for various data, especially unlabeled general QA data, the rewards are carefully designed, which is elaborated on in the following. We adopt accuracy and format rewards according to convention, and for a trajectory with the grounding action, we calculate a grounding-related reward to give feedback to the grounding action, where we design Fine-grained Grounding Reward and Self-Confirmed Pseudo Reward for the training sample with and without grounding labels, respectively. To avoid the optimization conflicts between accuracy and grounding, we apply the accuracy-gated mechanism to give higher priority to accuracy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Accuracy and Format Rewards.</span>
Following  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, the accuracy and format rewards are included. The accuracy reward evaluates the correctness of the answer in the last turn.</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(5)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{acc}}=\begin{cases}1.0\ \ \text{final answer is correct}\\
0.0\ \ \text{otherwise}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>acc</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>1.0</mn><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>final answer is correct</mtext></mrow></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mn>0.0</mn><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>otherwise</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{acc}}=\begin{cases}1.0\ \ \text{final answer is correct}\\
0.0\ \ \text{otherwise}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.2" class="ltx_p">The format reward evaluates if a trajectory follows the grounding or answering action format in all turns.</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{format}}=\begin{cases}0.2\ \ \text{all turns follow the right format}\\
0.0\ \ \text{otherwise}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>format</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0.2</mn><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>all turns follow the right format</mtext></mrow></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mn>0.0</mn><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>otherwise</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{format}}=\begin{cases}0.2\ \ \text{all turns follow the right format}\\
0.0\ \ \text{otherwise}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fine-grained Grounding Reward.</span>
For data with video grounding annotations, the <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{grounding}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>grounding</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{grounding}}</annotation></semantics></math> is calculated by</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E7X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="3" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_left">(7)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle R_{\mathrm{soft}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R_{\mathrm{soft}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\text{IoU}({{g_{\mathrm{last}}}},{g_{\mathrm{gt}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>IoU</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>gt</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\text{IoU}({{g_{\mathrm{last}}}},{g_{\mathrm{gt}}})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E7Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle R_{\mathrm{hard}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>hard</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R_{\mathrm{hard}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=0.5\cdot\mathbb{I}(\text{IoU}({{g_{\mathrm{last}}}},{{g_{\mathrm{gt}}}})&gt;0.0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>IoU</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>gt</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=0.5\cdot\mathbb{I}(\text{IoU}({{g_{\mathrm{last}}}},{{g_{\mathrm{gt}}}})&gt;0.0)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E7Xb" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7Xb.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle R_{\mathrm{grounding}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>grounding</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R_{\mathrm{grounding}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7Xb.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=R_{\mathrm{soft}}+R_{\mathrm{hard}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>hard</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=R_{\mathrm{soft}}+R_{\mathrm{hard}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p4.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{g_{\mathrm{last}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{g_{\mathrm{last}}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{g_{\mathrm{gt}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>gt</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{g_{\mathrm{gt}}}}</annotation></semantics></math> represent the last grounding action and the ground truth label. The complementary nature of these reward signals motivates their integration: <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{soft}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{soft}}</annotation></semantics></math> offers discriminative power yet is relatively weak, whereas <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{hard}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>hard</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{hard}}</annotation></semantics></math> delivers high-confidence guidance but is less discriminative. Their combination effectively offsets their respective limitations.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>. </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The illustration of our proposed TwG-GRPO algorithm.</span><span id="acmlabel3" class="ltx_acm_description ltx_centering ltx_nodisplay"></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Self-Confirmed Pseudo Reward.</span>
When dealing with large amounts of data without grounding labels, it is difficult to calculate <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{grounding}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>grounding</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{grounding}}</annotation></semantics></math> to evaluate the quality of the grounding action. Distinguishing between better and worse grounding actions is non-trivial, as it has been observed that the model can sometimes produce correct answers while grounding video clips that do not contribute to answering the question, leading to unnecessary computational overhead. To address this issue, we propose a Self-Confirmed Pseudo Reward to approximate the effect of <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{grounding}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>grounding</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{grounding}}</annotation></semantics></math> in encouraging high-quality grounding actions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The core idea is to use the model itself as the judge. Specifically, we prompt the model to answer the question <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> based solely on the last grounded video clip <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{last}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{last}}</annotation></semantics></math>. If the model can produce the correct answer using only this clip, then <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{last}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{last}}</annotation></semantics></math> is considered more likely to be helpful for answering <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> compared to when it fails to do so.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p7.1" class="ltx_p">In detail, for each trajectory containing grounding actions, let the last grounding action be <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\mathrm{last}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\mathrm{last}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the corresponding video clip be <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\mathrm{last}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\mathrm{last}}</annotation></semantics></math> (which follows the fine-grained video representation defined in Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1. Preliminary ‣ 3. Video-TwG Framework ‣ Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> so as to accelerate with cache), and the ground-truth answer be <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{\mathrm{gt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>gt</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{\mathrm{gt}}</annotation></semantics></math>. We prompt the policy model <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> to generate an answer using only <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{last}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{last}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{\prime}(Q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{\prime}(Q)</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is the prompt for this self-confirming instruction:</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(8)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\prime}=\mathcal{M}(v_{\mathrm{last}},p^{\prime}(Q))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>last</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\prime}=\mathcal{M}(v_{\mathrm{last}},p^{\prime}(Q)).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p7.2" class="ltx_p">Then, the <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{pseudo}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{pseudo}</annotation></semantics></math> is calculated through</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(9)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{pseudo}}=\begin{cases}0,&amp;\text{if the self-confirmed answer is correct},\\
-\gamma,&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>pseudo</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>if the self-confirmed answer is correct</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{pseudo}}=\begin{cases}0,&amp;\text{if the self-confirmed answer is correct},\\
-\gamma,&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p7.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> is a hyper-parameter, and the reward is implemented in the form of a penalty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Accuracy-Gated Mechanism.</span>
Since the correctness of the answer is of higher priority. Accordingly, the grounding-related reward is awarded only if the trajectory leads to a correct final answer to avoid the optimization conflict.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Above all, the reward can be calculated by</p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(10)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=\begin{cases}R_{\text{acc}}+R_{\text{format}},&amp;\text{(a)}\\[4.0pt]
R_{\text{acc}}+R_{\text{format}}+\mathbb{I}(R_{\text{acc}}&gt;0)\cdot R_{\text{grounding}},&amp;\text{(b)}\\[4.0pt]
R_{\text{acc}}+R_{\text{format}}+\mathbb{I}(R_{\text{acc}}&gt;0)\cdot R_{\text{pseudo}},&amp;\text{(c)}\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>acc</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>format</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext>(a)</mtext></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>acc</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>format</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>acc</mtext></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>grounding</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext>(b)</mtext></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>acc</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>format</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>acc</mtext></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>pseudo</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext>(c)</mtext></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=\begin{cases}R_{\text{acc}}+R_{\text{format}},&amp;\text{(a)}\\[4.0pt]
R_{\text{acc}}+R_{\text{format}}+\mathbb{I}(R_{\text{acc}}&gt;0)\cdot R_{\text{grounding}},&amp;\text{(b)}\\[4.0pt]
R_{\text{acc}}+R_{\text{format}}+\mathbb{I}(R_{\text{acc}}&gt;0)\cdot R_{\text{pseudo}},&amp;\text{(c)}\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p9.2" class="ltx_p">where (a), (b), and (c) correspond to trajectories without grounding actions, with grounding actions for labeled GQA data, and with grounding actions for general QA data, respectively. Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 3.5. TwG-GRPO Algorithm ‣ 3. Video-TwG Framework ‣ Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows the reward calculation briefly.</p>
</div>

            <span id="alg1.l5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg1.l5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\ \text{{in}}\ 1,...,K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">in</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn> 1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\ \text{{in}}\ 1,...,K</annotation></semantics></math>  <span id="alg1.l5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l6" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">6:</span></span>
              
              
              <math id="alg1.l6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{k}\leftarrow\mathcal{M}_{\theta}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{k}\leftarrow\mathcal{M}_{\theta}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l6.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="alg1.l6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Get the current output.
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">7:</span></span>
              
              
              <span id="alg1.l7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> matches "grounding" format <span id="alg1.l7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>

</div>

<td id="S4.T1.9.16.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.16.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">47.3<sub id="S4.T1.9.16.8.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S4.T1.9.16.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">4.8↑</span></sub></span></td>

<td id="S4.T1.9.16.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.16.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">54.6<sub id="S4.T1.9.16.11.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S4.T1.9.16.11.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">7.1↑</span></sub></span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T1.9.17" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S4.T1.9.17.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">71.2</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">53.8</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">46.7</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">57.2</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">63.5</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">69.8</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">49.5</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="font-size:90%;">45.6</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">52.4</span></td>
<td id="S4.T1.9.17.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.17.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">55.3</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T1.9.18" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S4.T1.9.18.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T1.9.18.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">71.9<sub id="S4.T1.9.18.2.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S4.T1.9.18.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">0.7↑</span></sub></span></td>
